title: Report On Lan Yui Mung

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
C. I. D. REGISTER
No. I. C. D. 684
Lai Mi Bung
Date 27. 1. 30.

Translation of a letter from C.D.C. 93
addressed to the D.C.I.:-

Sir,

I beg to report that at 6.30 p.m. on
December 27 I was invited by one Yen Feng San
to the latter's house at Sin Kai Woo. When I
arrived there I saw more than 20 men in the house.
I was then taken by them to Room No. 28 of the Lee
Bing lodging house in the neighbourhood of Sin Kai
Woo, where I was detained. At 10 a.m. on the
following morning they asked me to go to a teashop.
When they took me into Chinese Territory they called
a policeman who accompanied us to the Shanghai
District Court. Upon arriving at the Court the
complainant informed the Court that I have
fraudulently claimed to be a comprador of a steamer
belonging to the Butterfield & Swire & Co. I told
the Court that some time in the month of May Mr.
Jamieson, British Consul, introduced me to the
Butterfield & Swire & Co. and Jardine & Matheson & Co.,
and documents referring to this are now on file for
reference purposes.

The Court then told me that if the British
Consul will testify my statement I shall be released.

( This report is made in detention house No. 29,
Shanghai District Court, on December 29, 1929 )

Ruff
JAN 21 1930
31/1 '2
21/1

日期 1930年1月27日

第93号华籍侦探致副总监函件的译文：-

先生，

谨此报告，12月27日下午6时30分，我受严凤三（Yen Feng San）邀请前往其位于新河（Sin Kai Woo）的住所。抵达后，我看见屋内有二十余人。随后，他们将我带至新河附近的李炳（Lee Bing）客栈28号房间，并将我拘禁于此。次日上午10时，他们要求我去一家茶馆。当他们把我带入华界时，叫来了一名警察，该警察陪同我们前往上海地方法院。到达法院后，原告向法庭指控我欺诈性地声称自己是太古洋行（Butterfield & Swire & Co.）所属轮船的买办。我告诉法庭，今年五月某时，英国领事詹姆森先生（Mr. Jamieson）将我引荐给太古洋行和怡和洋行（Jardine & Matheson & Co.），有关此事的文件现已存档备查。

法庭随后告知我，如果英国领事能证明我的陈述属实，我将获释。

（本报告于1929年12月29日在上海地方法院第29号拘留所作出）

Ruff
1930年1月21日

21/1

C.I.D. Headquarter staff Station.

December 31st., 1929.

Further REPORT ON C.D.C. 92 Lan Yui Mung Imprisoned in the Chinese
City for Fraud.

Made by and Forwarded by D.S.I. Telfer

Sir,
C.D.S.I. Voong Pah Zung called at the Chinese City Court
on December 30th, 1929, for C.D.C. 92 Lan Yui Mung's "Warrant
Card", but the authorities there would not hand over same to
him until a foreigner made application for it. This infor-
mation was forwarded to you on the morning of December 31st.,
1929, and I understand Tan Zau Liang of the Chinese Intelli-
gence Office has been instructed to make the necessary appli-
cation.

C.D.C. 134 Voong Shih Foo went to interview Yoong Kai
Nan(楊梅南), comprador of Butterfield & Swire, The French
Bund, at his office at latter address on December 31st., 1929,
re C.D.C. 92 Lan Yui Mung. He informed him that Lan Yui Mung
had given great assistance to the foreign community in Sze-
chuen during the trouble in 1925, consequently he had to leave
as the Chinese were taking up a dangerous attitude against him.
He left and came to Shanghai eventually. Mr. W. F. Johnstone,
then the manager of the above shipping company's Branch in
Szechuen, wrote a letter to the manager of the Shanghai Branch
to give Lan Yui Mung a position. Owing to the fact the latter
had no experience in the shipping business and had no guaran-
tor the manager in Shanghai could not give him a job. The
story that Lan Yui Mung would be taken on with the aforemen-
tioned shipping company as comprador was groundless.

I am, Sir,
Yours obediently
Alexander Telfer
D.S.I.

A/D.C.I.

1929年12月31日。

关于华籍侦探第92号兰玉明（Lan Yui Mung）因欺诈罪被囚禁于华界的进一步报告。

由副督察特尔弗（Telfer）撰写并呈报

先生，
华籍副督察冯柏宗（Voong Pah Zung）于1929年12月30日前往华界法院索取华籍侦探第92号兰玉明的“拘票卡”，但当局表示除非有外国人提出申请，否则不予移交。此信息已于1929年12月31日上午转达给您，据我了解，已指示华人情报办公室的谭佐良（Tan Zau Liang）进行必要的申请。

华籍侦探第134号冯世富（Voong Shih Foo）于1929年12月31日前往法外滩太古洋行买办杨梅南（Yoong Kai Nan）的办公室，就华籍侦探第92号兰玉明一事与其面谈。他告知冯，兰玉明在1925年动乱期间曾对四川的外侨社区提供极大帮助，因此由于中国人对他采取危险态度，他不得不离开。他最终离开并来到上海。当时上述航运公司四川分行的经理W. F. Johnstone先生曾写信给上海分行经理，要求给兰玉明安排一个职位。鉴于后者缺乏航运业务经验且无担保人，上海经理无法给他提供工作。所谓兰玉明将被上述航运公司聘为买办的说法毫无根据。

先生，
您忠顺的仆人
亚历山大·特尔弗
副督察

代理副总监

C.I.D. Headquarters Station.
December 29th, 1929.

REPORT ON C.D.C. 92 Lan Yui Hung imprisoned in the
Chinese City for Fraud.

Made by and Forwarded by D.S.I. Telfer

Sir,
I beg to report that C.D.C. 92 Lan Yui Hung failed to '
appear at the Special Criminal Branch office on the morning
of December 28th, 1929. C.D.C. 1 Chang Sau Ching was sent
to the aforementioned detective's home at No.586 Yunnan Road
to inquire for him.
C.D.C. 1 Chang Sau Ching did not find him at his home,
but ascertained from the Chinese who live there that he had
been arrested by the French Police on the afternoon of De-
cember 27, 1929.
Enquiries were made at the French Police, but it was
discovered he had not been arrested by them.
It was later ascertained that a Chinese named Nyi Voong
San(倪凤山) living at No.37 French Bund detained C.D.C. 92
Lan Yui Hung at the latter address on his own authority on
December 27, 1929, about 7 p.m., and then took him to the Chi-
nese District Court, Chinese City, on Dec. 29,1929, for Fraud.
From enquiries made from Nyi Voong San it was ascertained
that C.D.C. 92 Lan Yui Hung between April 1929 and October
1929 had collected over $2000 from 41 Chinese as guarantee
money for jobs on the s/s "Tai tung" owned by Butterfield &
Swire. He had informed those Chinese that he was compradore
on this particular steamship and had got his position through
the British Consul. This they believed, because he was seen
to go several times to the British Consulate. However, on
the Chinese Festival of the 8th moon(September 17th 1929) when

关于华籍侦探第92号兰玉洪（Lan Yui Hung）因欺诈罪被囚禁于华界的报告。

由副督察特尔弗（Telfer）撰写并呈报

先生，
谨此报告，华籍侦探第92号兰玉洪未于1929年12月28日上午出现在特别刑案股办公室。华籍侦探第1号张守清（Chang Sau Ching）被派往上述侦探位于云南路586号的家中查询其下落。
华籍侦探第1号张守清在其家中未找到他，但从居住在那里的中国人处获悉，他已于1929年12月27日下午被法国警察逮捕。
经向法国警察查询，发现他并未被法警逮捕。
后经查明，一名居住在法外滩37号、名为倪凤山（Nyi Voong San）的中国人，于1929年12月27日晚7时许，擅自将华籍侦探第92号兰玉洪拘禁于上述地址，随后于1929年12月29日将其带至华界上海地方法院，指控其犯有欺诈罪。
经向倪凤山查询得知，华籍侦探第92号兰玉洪在1929年4月至1929年10月期间，以担保太古洋行所属“泰通”号（Tai tung）轮船职位为由，从41名中国人处收取了超过2000美元的保证金。他告知这些中国人他是该特定轮船的买办，并通过英国领事获得了该职位。这些人相信了他的话，因为有人看见他多次前往英国领事馆。然而，在中秋节（1929年9月17日）时，当

他承诺将给予这41名中国人“泰丰”号（Taifung）轮船上的职位时；他并未履行承诺，因而拖延了如此长的时间，致使他们意识到他是一个骗子。

这41名中国人已向华界法院提出控告，因此他因涉嫌欺诈罪在那里被捕候审。

华籍副督察冯柏宗将于1929年12月30日前往华界法院索取华籍侦探第92号兰玉坤（Lan Yui Kung）的拘票卡，并将同时告知当局，租界警方对他所受的指控不感兴趣。

D.C.I. from C.D.C. Lai Yu Ming, who is

District Court:

Sir,

I beg to report that two persons named Yih
Hai Chuen and Yen Feng San have instituted a lawsuit
against me at the Shanghai District Court accusing me
of having fraudulently claimed to be compradore of
Butterfield & Swire & Co.

After hearing the case the Judge of the
District Court ordered me to secure a letter from the
British Consul in order to testify my statement. If
I can succeed in securing this letter the Court will
release me at once.

Dated December 31, 1929.

J.C.

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL
OFFICE OF THE INSPECTORATE-GENERAL,
No. I. Q. D. 684.    SHANGHAI.
Date 14th December, 1929.

My dear Martin,

Many thanks for your letter of 3rd December,
(No. 10.D-684) Lui Yu Len has again called on me
this morning, with the letter, which I enclose in the
original, and do not want back. You will see that
he is now anxious to accept a salary of $23.

If therefore you are ready to reconsider your
decision and to give him a trial we shall be grate-
ful; if only to save us from his constant visitations!

But I leave it, of course, to you to take such
action as you think proper.

I am sending this letter sealed, and by the
hand of the individual concerned.

Yours sincerely,

Captain A.L.J.H. Martin,
Deputy Commissioner,
Shanghai Municipal Police.
Shanghai.

亲爱的马丁：

非常感谢您12月3日的来信，
(编号 10.D-684) Lui Yu Len（音译）今天上午再次带着随信附上的原件拜访了我，该原件无需退回。您会看到，他现在急于接受23美元的薪水。

因此，如果您愿意重新考虑您的决定并给予他试用机会，我们将不胜感激；哪怕只是为了让我们免受他的频繁造访之苦！

当然，我留待您采取认为适当的行动。

此信密封，并由当事人亲自送达。

您真诚的，

A.L.J.H. 马丁上尉，
副警务处长，
上海公共租界工部局警务处。
上海。

page_data.en:
4th December, 1929,
Shanghai.

Council General:
Great Britian,
Shanghai.

Sir,
I am much indebted you of your kind
favour to recommend me as a detective to the
police department of the Municipal Council.
I have been two times in the Municipal Council
and knowing that the salary of a detective is
twenty-three dollars per month, so I am ready
to take that post for my present living being.

Yesterday, I met with the foreign detective
in charge and he told me that he will consult
with you again because he thinks that the salary
of a detective can not help my living. There
must be something misunderstanding of the
foreign detective in charge. So now, I take
the liberty to let you know that there is no
objection of mine by taking that post even the
salary may not help me all.
page_data.zh:
1929年12月4日，
上海。

大不列颠驻上海
总领事馆：

先生，
承蒙您好意推荐我担任工部局警务处的侦探，不胜感激。
我曾两次前往工部局，得知侦探的月薪为二十三美元，因此为了维持目前的生计，我愿意接受该职位。

昨天，我见到了负责的外国侦探，他告诉我他将再次与您商议，因为他认为侦探的薪水不足以维持我的生活。负责的这位外国侦探一定有什么误会。因此，我现在冒昧让您知道，即使薪水不能完全维持我的生活，我也没有异议接受该职位。

page_data.en:
As you know I have done my best
in the volunteer of Szechuen and I hope
there will be a chance for me to undertake
an unexpected result to the secret service
of the Municipal Council by a special
appointment for me to run all over inside the
settlement.

I hope you would kindly helping me
to get that post by explaining my acceptness
of that post to the foreign detective in charge.

I thank you very much with all
my indebtedness.

Yours most obedient servant,
Lui Yu Mang 陸禹馬印
page_data.zh:
如您所知，我在四川的志愿工作中已竭尽全力，我希望有机会通过特别任命，让我在租界内四处活动，从而为工部局的秘密服务带来意想不到的成果。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
C. I. D. REGISTRY
No. I. O. D..684..
Date..4..12..29.

December 3, 29.

My dear Blunt,

With reference to your letter of November 2, Lui Yu Men has been carefully examined by our C.I.D. with a view to ascertaining his suitability or otherwise for employment in that department. He is, as you say, quite illiterate and further has rather exaggerated ideas of the price which should be paid for his services.

We have come to the conclusion that he is not suitable for employment as a detective and in consequence I am afraid we have nothing else to offer.

Yours sincerely, .

(Sgd) R. F. Maxwell

A. P. Blunt, Esq., C.M.G.,
H. B. M. Consul,
Shanghai.

1929年12月3日。

亲爱的 Blunt，

关于您11月2日的来信，我们的刑事侦缉处已对 Lui Yu Men（音译）进行了仔细审查，以确定他是否适合在该部门任职。正如您所说，他完全是个文盲，此外，他对自身服务应得报酬的想法有些夸大。

我们得出的结论是，他不适合受雇为侦探，因此恐怕我们无法提供其他职位。

您真诚的， .

（签名） R. F. Maxwell

A. P. Blunt 先生， C.M.G.,

General Remarks

The subject of attached letter has been examined
by D.I. Sung Daw & myself, & I am of the
opinion that he is not suitable for the
position of detective in the S.M.P. He has no
knowledge of Police duties or the Shanghai dialect,
and is a poorly educated person, he also expects
more remuneration than the present Salary of a 1st class
detective sergeant. Lew Yui Hung (雷惠門) states
that he has resided in Shanghai about 1 year,
& has been receiving about $ 300 monthly from
3 British shipping companies & the British
Consulate which ceased about 2 or 3 months ago.
He formerly received $ 200 monthly whilst serving as
an officer in the Chinese Army.

MUNICIPAL POLICE
I. D. REGISTRY
BRITISH CONSULATE-GENERAL 684
26. 11. 29.
SHANGHAI.
November 22nd, 1929.

My dear Martin,

I spoke to you on the telephone a
day or two ago about one Lui (Lei) Yu Men. I
will send him around to you with a chit in a
day or two, but in the meanwhile the following
are some details about him:-

2. He was Captain of the Lung Men Hao
(Chungking) "T'uan" or militia, at the time of
the disturbances of 1925 resulting from the
Shanghai May 30th affair. (Lung Men Hao, as
you probably know, is the suburb of Chungking
on the river bank opposite the town, where most
of the British mercantile community reside].
It was, to a considerable extent, due to Lui
(Lei) Yu Men that we did not have a really
serious/

Captain R.M.J.Martin,
Deputy Commissioner,
Shanghai Municipal Police.
SHANGHAI.
page_data.zh:
公共租界工部局警务处
刑事侦缉处登记室
英国总领事馆 684号
1929年11月26日。
上海。
1929年11月22日。

亲爱的马丁：

一两天前我在电话里跟你谈过一个叫 Lui (Lei) Yu Men 的人。我将在这一两天内让他带张便条去见你，但与此同时，以下是关于他的一些详情：-

2. 在1925年因上海五卅惨案引发的骚乱期间，他是龙门浩（重庆）“团”或民团的团长。（正如你可能知道的，龙门浩是重庆位于江对岸、与城区相对的郊区，大多数英国商界人士居住于此。）在很大程度上，多亏了 Lui (Lei) Yu Men，我们在龙门浩才没有发生真正严重的/

R.M.J. 马丁上尉，
副总监，
上海公共租界工部局警务处。
上海。

page_data.en:
2.
serious affair at Lung Men Hao. He took consider-
able risk and intervened frequently on behalf of the
British community. His action was, no doubt,
partly influenced by the fact that he and his militia
were subsidized by the British firms who had property
at that place.
3. After things had quietened down in the
autumn of 1925, he was deprived of his post as Capt-
ain of the militia owing to his friendliness to us.
An attempt was also made to murder him for the same
reason. Various British firms did their best to
give him employment, but on each occasion he proved
to be too big for his boots and he had to leave.
4. As to his subsequent history, I am not too
clear. I know that various concerns, Mackenzie
and Company, Asiatic Petroleum Company, Butterfield
and Swire and Jardine Matheson and Company have tried
to help him from time to time with money or other-
wise. Late in 1927 he appeared again in Chungking
and/
page_data.zh:
2.
严重事件。他承担了相当大的风险，并多次代表英国社群进行干预。毫无疑问，他的行动部分受到以下事实的影响：他和他的民团接受了在该地拥有财产的英国公司的津贴。
3. 1925年秋局势平息后，由于他对我们的友好态度，他被免去了民团团长的职务。出于同样的原因，还有人企图谋杀他。各家英国公司尽力为他安排工作，但每次他都显得眼高手低，不得不离职。
4. 至于他随后的经历，我不太清楚。我知道麦肯锡公司（Mackenzie and Company）、亚细亚火油公司（Asiatic Petroleum Company）、宝丰洋行（Butterfield and Swire）以及怡和洋行（Jardine Matheson and Company）等机构曾不时以金钱或其他方式试图帮助他。1927年末，他再次出现在重庆，并且/

page_data.en:
3.

and I got him a job as Staff Officer to one of the
local Generals. As far as I can understand his
story, he had to resign his post owing to the old
threats to himself. One of his friends was murder-
ed, and he was given a strong hint that if he stayed
at Chungking the same thing would happen to him.
At any rate, whatever was the cause of his leaving, I
understand that he will not go back to Chungking on
any account. He has addressed various petitions
to the British firms; to ourselves; to the Secretary
of State for Foreign Affairs and, I rather gather,
to yourselves (letter of June 1st 1929 to "British
Consul"), trying to get employment. Hence this letter
to you.

5. He is a Szechuanese; I gather largely
illiterate; and on his record, apart from the services
he rendered at Lung Men Hao, his work is not too re-
liable. His merits are that he is a good executive
officer with considerable personal courage and you
might/
page_data.zh:
3.

我帮他谋得了一份当地某位将军的参谋职务。据我对其陈述的理解，由于先前针对他个人的威胁，他不得不辞职。他的一位朋友被杀害，有人强烈暗示他，如果留在重庆，同样的事情也会发生在他身上。无论如何，无论他离开的原因是什么，据我了解，他绝不会以任何理由返回重庆。他曾向各家英国公司、向我们、向英国外交大臣，以及据我推测，也向你们（1929年6月1日致“英国领事”的信）递交过多份请愿书，试图谋求职位。故此致函于你。

5. 他是四川人；据我了解，他很大程度上是文盲；除了他在龙门浩提供的服务外，根据其履历，他的工作表现不太可靠。他的优点是作为一名执行军官表现出色，具备相当的个人勇气，而你或许/

page_data.en:
4.

might be able to find useful employment for him in
your detective branch.

6. As you will gather, I do not know sufficient
about the man to give him any personal recommendation.
But if you can give him any employment on trial, I
should be much obliged. I am telling him that
the shit I am giving him to you is the last thing we
can do for him.

Yrs. ever
Arthur
page_data.zh:
4.

或许能在你的侦探部门为他找到有用的工作。

6. 如你所知，我对这个人了解不足，无法给予任何个人推荐。但如果你能试用他，我将不胜感激。我告诉他，我给你这张便条是我们能为他做的最后一件事了。

永远是你的
阿瑟

I spoke to you on the telephone a

will send him around to you with a chit ina 
day or two, but in the meanwhile the following 
are some details about him:- 

2. He was Captain of the Lung Men Hao 
(Chungking) "T'uan" or militia, at the time of 
the disturbances of 1925 resulting from the 
Shanghai May 30th affair. (Lung Men Hao, as 
you probably know, is the suburb of Chungking 
on the river bank opposite the town, where most 
of the British mercantile community resicej. 
It was, to a considerable extent, due to Luli 


(Lei) Yu Men that we did not have a really

serious affair at Lung Men Hao. He took consider-

British community. His action was, no doubt, 
partly influenced by the fact that he and his militia 
were subsidized by the British firms who had property 
at that place. 
3. After things had quietened down in the 
autumn of 1925, he was deprived of his post as Capt- | 
ain of the militia owing to his friendliness to us. 
An attempt was also made to murder him for the same 
reason. Various British firms 41d their best to 
give him employment, but on each occasion he proved 
to be too big for his boots and he had to leave. 
4. As to his subsequent history, I am not too 
clear. I know that various concerns, Mackenzie 
and Company, Asiatic Petroleum Company, Butterfield 
and Swire and Jardine Matheson and Company have tried 
to help him from time to time with money or other- 
wise. Late in 1927 he appeared again in Chungking
